statements.name: Statement of financial position — AASB 1060, Tier 2 simplified disclosures
statements.legal_reference: AASB 1060 General Purpose Financial Statements – Simplified Disclosures for For-Profit and Not-for-Profit Tier 2 Entities, paragraphs 35 to 44. Paragraph 35 lists the line items a statement of financial position presents as a minimum and paragraph 42 prescribes neither their order nor their format, so the lines below are those items in the order Australian practice prints them, classified current and non-current under paragraphs 37 to 41. Corporations Act 2001, s. 295 and s. 296 — the financial report of a company that has to prepare one comprises financial statements that comply with the accounting standards, which the AASB makes under s. 334. Biological assets (35(h)), non-controlling interests (35(p)) and the items held for sale of AASB 5 (35(r) and (s)) are not lines here, because the chart carries no account for them.

lines.name: Current assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraphs 37 to 39 — current and non-current assets are presented as separate classifications, an asset being current when it is expected to be realised within the operating cycle or twelve months, or is cash.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(a).

lines.name: Trade and other receivables
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(b). GST paid on purchases and the GST refund due from the ATO are receivables from the Commissioner and not current tax, which paragraph 35(m) keeps for income tax; the suspense account reports here while it is in debit.

lines.name: Inventories
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(d).

lines.name: Financial assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(c), the part realised within twelve months.

lines.name: Current tax assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(m) — assets for current tax, which in Australia is income tax.

lines.name: Other current assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 36 — an additional line item, relevant to an understanding of the entity's financial position: prepayments and deposits paid, which are neither receivables nor financial assets.

lines.name: Non-current assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraphs 37 and 39 — every asset that is not current is non-current.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(e). Right-of-use assets are presented within this line, beside the assets of the same nature, which AASB 16 allows where they are disclosed in the notes; each cost account has its accumulated depreciation on the next code so that one range reaches the carrying amount.

lines.name: Investment property
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(f).

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(g).

lines.name: Investments in associates
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(i).

lines.name: Investments in joint ventures
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(j).

lines.name: Financial assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(c), the part not realised within twelve months.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(n) — deferred tax assets are always classified as non-current.

lines.name: Current liabilities
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraphs 37, 40 and 41 — current and non-current liabilities are presented as separate classifications.

lines.name: Trade and other payables
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(k). GST collected, the activity statement payable to the ATO, deferred GST on imports and PAYG amounts withheld are owed to the Commissioner and are not income tax, so they report here and not under paragraph 35(m); the suspense account reports here while it is in credit.

lines.name: Financial liabilities
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(l), the part due within twelve months, the credit card among them.

lines.name: Current tax liabilities
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(m) — liabilities for current tax.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(o), the part expected to be settled within twelve months, employee leave among it.

lines.name: Non-current liabilities
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 41 — every liability that is not current is non-current.

lines.name: Financial liabilities
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(l), the part not due within twelve months.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(n).

lines.name: Provisions
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(o), the part not expected to be settled within twelve months.

lines.name: Net assets
lines.legal_reference: Not a line AASB 1060 lists: the subtotal an Australian statement of financial position prints above equity, which paragraph 36 allows. It equals total equity once the year is closed, and exceeds it by the profit of the year until then.

lines.name: Equity
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 35(q) — equity attributable to the owners of the parent; paragraph 44(f) asks for its classes, which are the three lines below.

lines.name: Issued capital
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 44(f) — classes of equity, such as paid-in capital.

lines.name: Reserves
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 44(f) — reserves.

lines.name: Retained earnings
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 44(f) — retained earnings, after the dividends paid that are booked beside them.

statements.name: Statement of profit or loss — AASB 1060, Tier 2 simplified disclosures, expenses by nature
statements.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraphs 52 and 58. Paragraph 52 lists the minimum line items — revenue, finance costs, the share of associates and joint ventures, tax expense, discontinued operations and profit or loss — and paragraph 58 requires an analysis of expenses by nature or by function, whichever is more relevant; this statement analyses them by nature, which a small company's ledger holds without any allocation. The share of the profit or loss of equity-accounted investments and discontinued operations are not lines here, because the chart carries no account for them.

lines.name: Revenue
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 52(a).

lines.name: Other income
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 56 — an additional line item: income that is not revenue from contracts with customers: interest, rent, grants, foreign exchange gains and gains on disposal.

lines.name: Raw materials, consumables and goods for resale used
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 58(a) — expenses analysed by their nature: purchases of materials and goods, freight inwards, import charges, the change in inventories and subcontractors.

lines.name: Employee benefits expense
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 58(a) — employee benefits costs.

lines.name: Depreciation and amortisation expense
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 58(a) — depreciation.

lines.name: Other expenses
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 58(a) — the other expenses by nature, foreign exchange losses and losses on disposal among them.

lines.name: Finance costs
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 52(b).

lines.name: Income tax expense
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 52(d) — tax expense.

lines.name: Profit for the year
lines.legal_reference: AASB 1060, paragraph 52(f) — profit or loss. The pack carries no item of other comprehensive income, so this is also the total comprehensive income of paragraph 52(i), which the paragraph allows to be called profit or loss.
